entries.text: The coppers smashed my father's printer when I was eight.
entries.raw_text: 1,The coppers smashed my father's printer when I was eight.

entries.text: I remember the hot, cling-film-in-a-microwave smell of it, and Da's look of ferocious concentration as  he filled it with fresh goop, and the warm, fresh-baked feel of the objects that came out of it.
entries.raw_text: 1,I remember the hot, cling-film-in-a-microwave smell of it, and Da's look of ferocious concentration as  he filled it with fresh goop, and the warm, fresh-baked feel of the objects that came out of it.

entries.text: The coppers came through the door with truncheons swinging, one of them reciting the terms of the warrant through a bullhorn.
entries.raw_text: 1,The coppers came through the door with truncheons swinging, one of them reciting the terms of the warrant through a bullhorn.

entries.text: One of Da's customers had  shopped him. The ipolice paid in high-grade pharmaceuticals -- performance enhancers, memory supplements, metabolic boosters.
entries.raw_text: 1,One of Da's customers had  shopped him. The ipolice paid in high-grade pharmaceuticals -- performance enhancers, memory supplements, metabolic boosters.

entries.text: The kind of thing that cost a fortune over the counter; the kind of thing you could print at home, if you didn't mind the risk of having your kitchen filled with a sudden crush of big, beefy bodies, hard truncheons whistling through the air, smashing anyone and anything that got in the way.
entries.raw_text: 1,The kind of thing that cost a fortune over the counter; the kind of thing you could print at home, if you didn't mind the risk of having your kitchen filled with a sudden crush of big, beefy bodies, hard truncheons whistling through the air, smashing anyone and anything that got in the way.

entries.text: They destroyed grandma's trunk, the one she'd brought from the old country.
entries.raw_text: 1,They destroyed grandma's trunk, the one she'd brought from the old country.

entries.text:
They smashed our little refrigerator and the purifier unit over the window.
My tweetybird escaped death by hiding in a corner of his cage as a big, booted foot crushed most of it into a sad tangle of printer-wire.

1,They smashed our little refrigerator and the purifier unit over the window. 
My tweetybird escaped death by hiding in a corner of his cage as a big, booted foot crushed most of it into a sad tangle of printer-wire.

entries.text: Da.
entries.raw_text: 1,Da.

entries.text: What they did to him.
entries.raw_text: 1,What they did to him.

entries.text: When he was done, he looked like he'd been brawling with an entire rugby side.
entries.raw_text: 1,When he was done, he looked like he'd been brawling with an entire rugby side.

entries.text: They brought him out the door and let the newsies get a good look at him as they tossed him in the car, while a spokesman told the world that my Da's organized-crime bootlegging operation had been responsible for at least twenty million in contraband, and that my Da, the desperate villain, had resisted arrest.
entries.raw_text: 1,They brought him out the door and let the newsies get a good look at him as they tossed him in the car, while a spokesman told the world that my Da's organized-crime bootlegging operation had been responsible for at least twenty million in contraband, and that my Da, the desperate villain, had resisted arrest.

entries.text: I saw it all from my phone, in the remains of the sitting room, watching it  on the screen and wondering how, just *how* anyone could look at our little flat and our terrible, manky estate and mistake it for the home of an organized crime kingpin.
entries.raw_text: 1,I saw it all from my phone, in the remains of the sitting room, watching it  on the screen and wondering how, just *how* anyone could look at our little flat and our terrible, manky estate and mistake it for the home of an organized crime kingpin.

entries.text: They took the printer away, of course, and displayed it like a trophy for the newsies.
entries.raw_text: 1,They took the printer away, of course, and displayed it like a trophy for the newsies.

entries.text: Its little shrine in the kitchenette seemed horribly empty.
entries.raw_text: 1,Its little shrine in the kitchenette seemed horribly empty.

entries.text: When I roused myself and picked up the flat and rescued my peeping poor tweetybird, I put a blender there.
entries.raw_text: 1,When I roused myself and picked up the flat and rescued my peeping poor tweetybird, I put a blender there.

entries.text: It was made out of  printed parts, so it would only last a month before I'd need to print new bearings and other moving parts.
entries.raw_text: 1,It was made out of  printed parts, so it would only last a month before I'd need to print new bearings and other moving parts.

entries.text: Back then, I could take apart and reassemble anything that could be printed.
entries.raw_text: 1,Back then, I could take apart and reassemble anything that could be printed.

entries.text: By the time I turned eighteen, they were ready to let Da out of prison.
entries.raw_text: 1,By the time I turned eighteen, they were ready to let Da out of prison.

entries.text: I'd visited him three times -- on my tenth birthday, on his fiftieth, and when Ma died.
entries.raw_text: 1,I'd visited him three times -- on my tenth birthday, on his fiftieth, and when Ma died.

entries.text: It had been two years since I'd last seen him and he was in bad shape.
entries.raw_text: 1,It had been two years since I'd last seen him and he was in bad shape.

entries.text: A prison fight had left him with a limp, and he looked over his shoulder so often it was like he had a tic.
entries.raw_text: 1,A prison fight had left him with a limp, and he looked over his shoulder so often it was like he had a tic.

entries.text: I was embarrassed when the minicab dropped us off in front of the estate, and tried to keep my distance from this ruined, limping skeleton as we went inside and up the stairs.
entries.raw_text: 1,I was embarrassed when the minicab dropped us off in front of the estate, and tried to keep my distance from this ruined, limping skeleton as we went inside and up the stairs.

entries.text: "Lanie," he said, as he sat me down.
entries.raw_text: 1,"Lanie," he said, as he sat me down.

entries.text: "You're a smart girl, I know that. Trig. You wouldn't know where your old Da could get a printer and some goop?"
entries.raw_text: 1,"You're a smart girl, I know that. Trig. You wouldn't know where your old Da could get a printer and some goop?"

entries.text: I squeezed my hands into fists so tight my fingernails cut into my palms.
entries.raw_text: 1,I squeezed my hands into fists so tight my fingernails cut into my palms.

entries.text: I closed my eyes.
entries.raw_text: 1,I closed my eyes.

entries.text: "You've been in prison for ten years, Da. Ten. Years."
entries.raw_text: 1,"You've been in prison for ten years, Da. Ten. Years."

entries.text: "You're going to risk another ten years to print out more blenders and pharma, more laptops and designer hats?"
entries.raw_text: 1,"You're going to risk another ten years to print out more blenders and pharma, more laptops and designer hats?"

entries.text: He grinned.
entries.raw_text: 1,He grinned.

entries.text: "I'm not stupid, Lanie."
entries.raw_text: 1,"I'm not stupid, Lanie."

entries.text: "I've learned my lesson."
entries.raw_text: 1,"I've learned my lesson."

entries.text: "There's no hat or laptop that's worth going to jail for."
entries.raw_text: 1,"There's no hat or laptop that's worth going to jail for."

entries.text: "I'm not going to print none of that rubbish, never again."
entries.raw_text: 1,"I'm not going to print none of that rubbish, never again."

entries.text: He had a cup of tea, and he drank it now like it was whisky, a sip and then a long, satisfied exhalation.
entries.raw_text: 1,He had a cup of tea, and he drank it now like it was whisky, a sip and then a long, satisfied exhalation.

entries.text: He closed his eyes and leaned back in his chair.
entries.raw_text: 1,He closed his eyes and leaned back in his chair.

entries.text: "Come here, Lanie, let me whisper in your ear."
entries.raw_text: 1,"Come here, Lanie, let me whisper in your ear."

entries.text: "Let me tell you the thing that I decided while I spent ten years in lockup."
entries.raw_text: 1,"Let me tell you the thing that I decided while I spent ten years in lockup."

entries.text: "Come here and listen to your stupid Da."
entries.raw_text: 1,"Come here and listen to your stupid Da."

entries.text: I felt a guilty pang about ticking him off.
entries.raw_text: 1,I felt a guilty pang about ticking him off.

entries.text: He was off his rocker, that much was clear.
entries.raw_text: 1,He was off his rocker, that much was clear.

entries.text: God knew what he went through in prison.
entries.raw_text: 1,God knew what he went through in prison.

entries.text: "What, Da?" I said, leaning in close.
entries.raw_text: 1,"What, Da?" I said, leaning in close.

entries.text: "Lanie, I'm going to print more printers. Lots more printers. One for everyone."
entries.raw_text: 1,"Lanie, I'm going to print more printers. Lots more printers. One for everyone."

entries.text: "That's worth going to jail for. That's worth anything."
entries.raw_text: 1,"That's worth going to jail for. That's worth anything."
